headline: Shimla Temperature: Himachal Likely To Get 2-3°C Hotter This Week, Yellow Alert In 2 Districts
content: Shimla Weather News: Himachal Pradesh continued to reel under rising temperatures on Tuesday, with Una recording the highest maximum temperature in the state at 43.4°C. Neri followed closely at 41.2°C, while Sundernagar registered 38.6°C. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD) in Shimla, maximum temperatures across the state are expected to rise further by 2-3 degrees over the next two to three days. Minimum temperatures are also likely to increase by a similar margin in several regions during the same period. Shimla recorded a maximum temperature of 29.4°C, which was 4.4 degrees above normal, while Dharamshala registered 35.1°C, nearly 3.9 degrees above the seasonal average. Several other stations, including Bhuntar, Manali, Mandi, Kalpa and Keylong, also reported above-normal daytime temperatures despite scattered rainfall in parts of the state. Light Rain Brings Temporary Relief In Hill Districts Some areas of Himachal Pradesh experienced brief relief from the heat on Tuesday as light rainfall was reported in parts of Chamba, Kangra, Kullu, Mandi, Shimla and Lahaul-Spiti districts. Light to moderate rain in higher reaches and mid-hill regions helped ease temperatures slightly. Manali recorded a maximum temperature of 28.5°C, while Keylong in Lahaul-Spiti settled at 21.8°C. However, despite isolated showers, temperatures remained above normal across most districts. The MeT department has predicted light rain and snowfall in parts of the state until May 25, particularly in middle and high hill areas. Plain regions are expected to witness largely dry conditions, except on May 22, when rainfall is likely across much of the state, as reported by Hindustan Times. Yellow Alert Issued For Heatwave Conditions The weather office has issued a yellow alert for heatwave conditions in Kangra and Solan districts for May 20 and 21, warning residents about rising daytime temperatures. Officials said dry weather prevailed across Himachal Pradesh over the last 24 hours. While minimum temperatures remained largely unchanged at several stations, some places recorded a rise of 2-5 degrees Celsius. Night temperatures also stayed above normal in many areas. Heatwave Impacts Himachal Farmers The ongoing heatwave has begun affecting daily life and agricultural activities in several districts. According to a report in The Indian Express, outdoor labourers and farmers engaged in cotton sowing and direct seeding of rice have been facing intense heat stress during daytime hours. The soaring temperatures have also impacted campaigning for upcoming municipal body elections, with candidates increasingly shifting public outreach activities to early mornings and evenings to avoid peak heat. The agriculture department has advised farmers to closely monitor vegetable crops for insect attacks and diseases, which tend to increase during hot weather conditions. Farmers have also been urged to carry out irrigation during evening hours to reduce heat stress on crops and conserve moisture. Additional recommendations include spreading straw mulch about 10 cm thick around plants and applying light irrigation in plant basins to retain soil moisture. Authorities have further advised residents and farm workers to avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, stay hydrated and drink sufficient water during the ongoing hot spell. Rainfall Deficit Persists Across Himachal Pradesh Despite recent showers, Himachal Pradesh continues to face an overall rainfall deficit this month. Between May 1 and May 19, the state recorded 36.3 mm rainfall against the normal average of 40.7 mm, reflecting an 11% shortfall. However, a few districts received surplus rainfall during the period. Shimla recorded the highest rainfall at 77.1 mm, which was 68% above normal. Mandi received 56.2 mm rainfall against the usual 40.9 mm, while Kangra recorded 55 mm compared to its normal of 33.7 mm.
